findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are stored in plaintext Lambda environment variables, visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration/describe permissions and committed to version control.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the service-owned default key rather than a customer-managed CMK with controllable key policy and rotation.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS.
The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no subnet/security-group controls, providing an unmonitored data exfiltration path.
No code_signing_config_arn is attached, so the deployment package is not signature-validated and tampering between build and deployment would go undetected.
